database_and_relations_policy.heading: Connect Information Once. Use It Across the Entire Workspace.
principles: Single Source of Truth: Store data entities (Clients, Projects, Tasks) in dedicated source databases; reference them via Relations rather than duplicating text records.
Relational Integrity: Establish clean two-way relations (Client → Projects, Project → Tasks); ensure parent-child associations remain unambiguous.
Rollup Discipline: Use Rollups to summarize connected progress (task completion counts, earliest start dates) without manual spreadsheet calculations.
Source Database vs Linked View: Understand that editing a linked database view modifies the underlying source record; filters only alter visual presentation, not data storage.
View Filters Are Not Permissions: Never rely on filtered database views (e.g., 'My Assigned Tasks') to secure confidential records; anyone with source database access can view all rows.

forms_and_automations_boundary.heading: Understand What Is Manual, What Is Automated, and What Requires a Paid Plan
principles: Notion Forms Access: Basic Forms are accessible across standard Notion plans; advanced styling and conditional branching require eligible paid tiers.
Buttons vs Automations: Interactive database buttons trigger actions upon manual clicks; automated event triggers (status change, date arrival) are primarily paid features.
Automation Trigger Constraints: Free-plan automations are restricted (e.g., basic Slack alerts); multi-step triggers and cascading automations require paid plans.
Manual Fallback Requirement: All required course projects can be completed using manual updates, templates, and basic buttons—no student is forced to buy a paid plan to graduate.

notion_ai_and_agents_governance.heading: AI Can Assist Your Workspace. Human Review Must Remain in Control.
principles: Awareness of October 2026 Architecture: Covers Notion Agents, custom agent scoping, MCP connections, and the updated credit model at a practical governance level.
Credit & Plan Awareness: Educates students on monthly AI credit allocations, transition timelines (October/November 2026), and administrative spending limits.
Mandatory Human Review: Crucial changes (client statuses, task assignees, contractual terms) must be verified through Agent Review Mode before committing.
Synthetic Data Policy: No real customer lists, confidential financial records, or PII are permitted in classroom AI prompts; students use synthetic business scenarios exclusively.

knowledge_base_and_sop_standards.heading: Keep Important Knowledge Findable, Reliable, and Easy to Maintain
principles: SOP Structural Standard: Every SOP requires a clear title, business purpose, named owner, preconditions, numbered steps, expected output, quality checks, and review date.
Searchable Categorization: Knowledge assets must include logical tags, breadcrumb hierarchies, and internal links to ensure rapid retrieval during team operations.
Maintenance & Deprecation: Stale procedures degrade operational trust; workspaces must include scheduled review cycles and archived legacy documentation.

curriculum.title: Notion Fundamentals & Information Structure
curriculum.objective: Understand Notion's page/block structure and design a logical, maintainable workspace.
lessons: 1.1 Introduction to Notion: Core productivity capabilities; Notes, docs, wikis, databases, project coordination, and team workspaces.
1.2 Workspace Concepts: Personal accounts vs team workspaces; Teamspaces; Private pages vs shared pages; Members and guest distinctions.
1.3 Notion Interface Mastery: Sidebar navigation; Quick find and search; Breadcrumb paths; Workspace settings awareness; Command palette.
1.4 Page Management: Creating pages; Renaming, moving, duplicating, archiving, and trashing pages; URL slug customization.
1.5 Block Architecture: The block foundation; Paragraphs, Headings (H1, H2, H3), bulleted lists, numbered lists, to-do checklists, quotes, and callouts.
1.6 Advanced Page Organization: Toggle lists and toggle headings; Multi-column layouts; Horizontal dividers; Internal page links; Linked mentions.
1.7 Nested Pages & Hierarchy: Parent and child page relationships; Constructing clear depth without confusing excessive nesting.
1.8 Information Architecture: Categorization logic; Primary navigation structures; Naming conventions; Content ownership and lifecycle.
1.9 Knowledge Organization: Segmenting company knowledge by department, project, client type, and standard procedure.
1.10 Page Linking & Cross-Referencing: Link to page blocks; Inline @page mentions; Weaving relational documentation webs.
1.11 Table of Contents: Generating dynamic navigation from heading tags within long-form operational documents.
1.12 Synced Blocks Awareness: Creating reusable content blocks; Synchronization mechanics across multiple pages; Safe editing practices.
1.13 Page Templates: Creating repeatable document templates for meeting notes, client briefings, and SOP outlines.
1.14 Template Quality & Design: Writing clear instructional placeholders, standard headers, and checklist prompts for team consistency.
1.15 Workspace Navigation Hub: Designing clean operational homepages linking Projects, Clients, Knowledge Base, and SOPs.
1.16 Information Retrieval Strategies: Search filters; Quick Find shortcuts; Navigation breadcrumbs; Maintaining bookmark hubs.
1.17 Workspace Usability Standards: Avoiding aesthetic clutter, decorative widgets, and unnecessary nesting; Prioritizing reading clarity.
1.18 Page Permissions Awareness: Private vs team access; Public web publishing risks; Inherited parent page permissions.
1.19 Page Version History: Reviewing edit history; Identifying contributor modifications; Restoring prior versions; Plan limitations.
1.20 Workspace Troubleshooting: Recovering mislaid pages; Resolving broken internal links; Consolidating duplicate documents.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Construct a complete fictional small-business workspace homepage with dedicated hubs for Home, Clients, Projects, Tasks, Knowledge Base, SOP Library, and Team Resources.
curriculum.security_considerations: Enforce private workspace defaults; prevent accidental public web sharing; establish clean parent-child permission inheritance.

curriculum.title: Databases & Views
curriculum.objective: Build structured Notion databases with appropriate properties, filters and views for business tracking.
lessons: 2.1 What Is a Notion Database?: Structured records vs freeform pages; Database rows as full Notion pages; Source database concept.
2.2 Database vs Simple Page: Determining when structured properties are required vs simple text documents; Avoiding database bloat.
2.3 Creating Databases: Full-page databases vs inline databases; Sourcing data; Configuration settings.
2.4 Database Properties: Title, Text, Number, Select, Multi-select, Status, Date, Person, Checkbox, URL, Email, Phone, and Files & Media.
2.5 Database Schema Design: Defining property semantics; Selecting optimal data types; Enforcing required fields; Standardizing property names.
2.6 Record Consistency & Hygiene: Enforcing status conventions (To Do, In Progress, Done); Date standards; Preventing missing inputs.
2.7 Table View Mastery: Column reordering, wrapping text, showing/hiding properties, sorting, filtering, and summary calculations.
2.8 Board View (Kanban): Grouping by status or owner; Managing task workflow stages; Card previews and visible property toggles.
2.9 Calendar View: Plotting date properties; Visualizing milestones and deadlines; Drag-and-drop rescheduling mechanics.
2.10 Timeline View: Multi-date project scheduling; Setting start and end dates; Visualizing dependencies (subject to plan availability).
2.11 List View: Clean, compact displays for document registries, reading lists, and straightforward meeting agendas.
2.12 Gallery View: Visual card layouts for team directories, portfolio assets, product catalogs, and client showcase cards.
2.13 Multi-Condition Filters: Constructing AND/OR filter groups; Filtering by status, assignee, priority, and dynamic date boundaries.
2.14 Sorting Strategies: Multi-level sorting (e.g., Priority descending, then Due Date ascending); Preserving predictable views.
2.15 Grouping & Sub-Grouping: Grouping boards and tables by status, client, or category; Collapsing empty groups.
2.16 Linked Database Views: Creating linked views across different pages; Filtering the central source database for local context.
2.17 Source Database vs Linked View: Single source of truth: confirming that edits in a linked view modify the master record directly.
2.18 Views Are Not Permissions: The fundamental security rule: filtering out records on a view does NOT prevent users from accessing the source database.
2.19 Database Templates: Creating reusable record templates with pre-configured properties, checklists, and boilerplate instructions.
2.20 Recurring Database Templates: Scheduling recurring task creation where supported; Setting automated generation intervals.
2.21 CSV Data Imports: Preparing structured CSV files; Column header formatting; Data type matching; Mapping imports into Notion.
2.22 CSV Data Quality Assurance: Eliminating duplicate records, blank required fields, malformed dates, and unmapped property types.
2.23 Operational Reporting Views: Configuring specialized views for Open Tasks, Overdue Items, High-Priority Blockers, and Next 7 Days.
2.24 Dashboard Usability & Layout: Combining multiple linked views onto an executive dashboard with clear headers and minimal clutter.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Build a comprehensive Task Management Database with 7 core properties. Configure Table, Board, Calendar, 'My Tasks', and Overdue views, demonstrating CSV import mapping and linked view instances.
curriculum.security_considerations: Demonstrate that linked views inherit source database permissions; do not store confidential compensation or HR records in shared databases without property-level access controls.

curriculum.title: Connected Work Systems
curriculum.objective: Build connected client, project and task systems using relations, rollups, introductory formulas and reusable operational documentation.
lessons: 3.1 Designing Connected Systems: Mapping business entity models; Establishing relational architecture; Eliminating duplicate data entry.
3.2 Identifying Business Entities: Clients, Projects, Tasks, Team Members, Meetings, and Standard Operating Procedures.
3.3 Database Cardinality: Understanding one-to-many relationships (One Client → Many Projects; One Project → Many Tasks).
3.4 Notion Relations: Creating Relation properties; Selecting target databases; Configuring one-way vs two-way relation syncing.
3.5 Relational Data Integrity: Connecting records accurately; Auditing orphan tasks; Resolving broken relational links.
3.6 Notion Rollups: Sourcing data across relations; Calculating counts, sums, averages, and displaying related properties.
3.7 Rollup Applications: Calculating total tasks per project, percentage of completed tasks, and extracting client names into task views.
3.8 Rollup Boundaries & Limitations: Understanding dependency on relation integrity, property data types, and permission context.
3.9 Notion Formula Fundamentals: Formula 2.0 architecture; Basic operators, property tokens, text concatenation, and numeric arithmetic.
3.10 Practical Formula Applications: Writing formulas for Overdue Warnings (if date < today and status != Done), Days Remaining, and Status Badges.
3.11 Formula Hygiene & Testing: Handling empty properties, testing edge cases, formatting conditional output, and optimizing readability.
3.12 Client Database Engineering: Creating client records with Client ID, Category, Contact Channel, Pipeline Status, and Account Owner.
3.13 CRM-Style Pipeline Architecture: Configuring stages: Lead, Qualified, Proposal Sent, Active Project, Retainer, and Closed/Archived.
3.14 CRM Scope & Boundaries: Operational client tracking vs enterprise CRM; Clarifying lack of native email blast and billing infrastructure.
3.15 Project Database Engineering: Sourcing Client relations, target delivery dates, project health status, and project owner fields.
3.16 Task Database Engineering: Linking tasks to parent projects, assigning individual owners, setting hard deadlines, and priority tags.
3.17 Connected Three-Tier System: Establishing the end-to-end Client → Project → Task relational loop with linked dashboard views.
3.18 Reusable System Templates: Designing standardized templates for New Client Onboarding, New Project Kickoff, and Meeting Minutes.
3.19 Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs): Structural requirements: Purpose, Owner, Prerequisites, Numbered Steps, QC, and Review Dates.
3.20 SOP Documentation Engineering: Writing clear, unambiguous operational procedures in Notion callouts, toggles, and checklists.
3.21 Searchable Company Knowledge Base: Creating hierarchical wikis, categorization tags, FAQ sections, and policy repositories.
3.22 Information Findability: Establishing keyword-rich headers, cross-document links, and verified document ownership metadata.
3.23 Knowledge Base Governance: Establishing review cadences, assigning doc owners, identifying stale SOPs, and archiving legacy pages.
3.24 Executive Operations Dashboard: Unifying active client pipeline cards, active project timelines, and urgent task lists into one hub.
3.25 Preventing Relational Bloat: Keeping relations lean; Avoiding redundant cross-linking between unrelated auxiliary databases.
3.26 Debugging Relations & Rollups: Troubleshooting circular links, blank rollup returns, formula type mismatches, and broken relations.
3.27 Synthetic Data Validation: Testing connected systems using fictional client companies, simulated projects, and synthetic task lists.
3.28 Workspace Maintainability: Auditing database performance, keeping property counts reasonable, and documenting system schemas.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Engineer a connected small-business work system: build Client, Project, and Task databases linked by Relations and Rollups, implement overdue status formulas, construct an SOP library, and assemble an integrated operational dashboard.
curriculum.security_considerations: Do not replicate confidential client contracts or real financial data; ensure test relations are populated with synthetic business records exclusively.

curriculum.title: Collaboration & Automation
curriculum.objective: Configure appropriate collaboration and learn practical, safe workflow enhancements through forms, buttons and plan-dependent automations.
lessons: 4.1 Team Collaboration in Notion: Shared workspace etiquette; Teamspaces; Co-authoring; Asynchronous task coordination.
4.2 Inline Comments & Discussions: Commenting on specific text blocks; Replying in threads; Resolving discussions; Editing comments.
4.3 Mentions & Notifications: Using @person to assign accountability; Using @date for reminders; Using @page for inline reference.
4.4 Members vs Guests: Workspace membership roles; Guest invitations to specific pages; Managing seat limits and guest access bounds.
4.5 Sharing Modes: Private pages; Internal workspace sharing; Restricting to specific members; External guest access; Public web sharing.
4.6 Permission Levels: Full Access, Can Edit, Can Edit Content (database specific), Can Comment, and Can View.
4.7 Least-Privilege Access Management: Granting minimum necessary rights; Restricting Full Access to workspace administrators; Auditing guests.
4.8 Permission Inheritance Mechanics: Understanding how subpages inherit parent page permissions; Breaking inheritance safely.
4.9 Database Permissions Governance: Managing access to central source databases vs child pages; Property-level access awareness.
4.10 Security Myth: Filters vs Access: Reinforcing that database filters NEVER restrict underlying record access for users with database rights.
4.11 Advanced Access Controls Awareness: Page-level locking, property/column-level access (Business/Enterprise plan awareness).
4.12 Notion Forms Architecture: Creating intake forms connected directly to databases; Defining question fields; Setting required prompts.
4.13 Form Privacy & Settings: Anonymous response collection; Restricting form access to internal members vs external respondents.
4.14 Notion Forms Availability: Free-tier basic form capabilities vs paid-tier advanced customization and conditional question branching.
4.15 Form-to-Database Intake Workflow: Automatic row insertion upon submission; Routing requests to triage views; Assigning task owners.
4.16 Notion Buttons Fundamentals: Button blocks on pages vs database buttons; Understanding user-initiated manual trigger actions.
4.17 Button Plan Availability: Free-plan button actions (adding pages, editing properties) vs paid advanced multi-step actions.
4.18 Applied Button Exercises: Building 'Mark Complete' buttons, 'Create Meeting Note' buttons, and 'Open Linked Document' buttons.
4.19 Database Automations Overview: Triggers, conditions, and actions; Event-driven automation vs manual button clicks.
4.20 Automation Triggers: Page added; Property edited (e.g., Status changed to 'Done'); Date-based recurring triggers.
4.21 Automation Actions: Auto-updating properties (e.g., setting Completion Date to Today), adding related tasks, sending notifications.
4.22 Paid Plan Automation Boundaries: Clarifying that full database automations predominantly require Plus, Business, or Enterprise tiers.
4.23 Automation Limitations & Governance: Recognizing that automations do not natively chain infinitely; Testing action failures.
4.24 Workflow Testing & Quality Assurance: Testing form inputs, button triggers, permission barriers, and handling duplicate records.
4.25 Manual Fallback Standard: Designing bulletproof manual fallback procedures (checklists, templates) so systems function without paid automations.
4.26 Cost & Plan Awareness: Auditing team subscription costs, add-on features, credit limits, and external tool dependencies.
4.27 Access Auditing & Security Governance: Conducting quarterly guest reviews, revoking stale public links, and isolating confidential records.
4.28 Version History & Disaster Recovery: Recovering accidentally deleted databases, inspecting revision logs, and restoring previous versions.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Build a client intake and task routing workflow: connect a Notion Form to a Client intake database, configure review status tags, implement a 'Complete Task' database button, design a permission matrix for 4 roles, and document manual fallback rules.
curriculum.security_considerations: Paid database automations are never required for course completion; students must verify manual fallback procedures and audit guest sharing boundaries.

curriculum.title: Notion AI & Agents
curriculum.objective: Understand how Notion AI and AI agents can assist knowledge work while respecting costs, permissions, review and approval requirements.
lessons: 5.1 Notion AI Overview: Capabilities across workspace search, writing assistance, summarization, and automated database properties.
5.2 AI Architecture & Tiers: Notion Agent, Custom Agents, Q&A workspace search, AI database autofill, and plan-dependent availability.
5.3 AI Workspace Search: Natural language querying across company documentation; Inspecting cited source pages for factual veracity.
5.4 AI-Assisted Content Drafting: Drafting SOP outlines, meeting summaries, project kickoff notes, and initial knowledge base articles.
5.5 AI Database Autofill: Auto-summarizing project pages, generating action-item checklists, and auto-tagging categories in databases.
5.6 AI Agent Concepts: Autonomous vs assisted agents; Defining goals, contextual scope, available tools, permissions, and human oversight.
5.7 The Notion Agent: Workspace-wide assistance; Answering contextual questions, drafting documentation, and suggesting next steps.
5.8 Custom Agents Awareness: Scoping custom agents for specific workflows; Defining data access boundaries and task parameters.
5.9 October 2026 Agent Updates: Expanded context processing, cross-app connected workflows, MCP support, and Agent Review Mode.
5.10 Agent Review Mode & Approval Controls: Reviewing proposed database edits before committing; Rejecting erroneous agent actions.
5.11 Model Context Protocol (MCP) Awareness: External tool connections; Context exchange boundaries; Token consumption and data security.
5.12 Connection Safety & Access Hygiene: Restricting external tool connections; Limiting permissions to read-only where appropriate.
5.13 Credit System & Consumption Models: Standard vs Select credits; Monthly credit allowances; Administrative budget caps.
5.14 October/November 2026 Credit Transition: Rollout timelines (Oct 19 for new eligible workspaces; Nov 2 for existing); Account verification.
5.15 AI Budgeting & Cost Governance: Monitoring team credit burn rates; Disabling unapproved AI add-ons; Setting workspace spending limits.
5.16 AI Hallucinations in Operations: Identifying fabricated company policies, false task deadlines, incorrect client statuses, and math errors.
5.17 Factual Verification Protocol: Cross-referencing AI outputs against primary documentation; Verifying dates, assignees, and financial terms.
5.18 Sensitive Data Protection: Strict prohibition against pasting non-public enterprise contracts, employee records, or PII into AI prompts.
5.19 The Human-in-the-Loop Standard: Mandatory rule: AI proposes, human reviews and verifies, authorized user approves and commits.
5.20 Responsible Classroom AI Labs: Evaluating synthetic AI-generated SOPs, identifying deliberate errors, and executing manual corrections.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Conduct a supervised AI output audit on 3 synthetic workplace drafts (an SOP, a client update, and a task prioritization list). Identify hallucinations, correct errors, and document an operational AI governance checklist.
curriculum.deliverable: Responsible Notion AI & Agent Governance Checklist
curriculum.security_considerations: Notion AI is strictly optional; students never purchase AI plans or deploy unsupervised autonomous agents on real organizational data.

curriculum.title: Workspace Capstone
curriculum.objective: Integrate all course skills into a tested, secure and maintainable small-business Notion workspace.
lessons: 6.1 Small-Business Scenario Brief: Reviewing company profile, team roles, service offerings, clients, projects, and operational pain points.
6.2 Workspace Architecture Construction: Building the central homepage hub, establishing clean teamspace navigation, and organizing subpages.
6.3 Client Database Implementation: Sourcing client records, pipeline stages, contact channels, and account owners using synthetic data.
6.4 Project Database Engineering: Configuring project stages, start/target dates, priorities, and two-way relations to the Client database.
6.5 Task Database Engineering: Creating task records linked to projects, assigning team members, setting due dates, and priority tags.
6.6 Relations & Rollup Verification: Auditing all cross-database links; Verifying project task counts and completion percentage rollups.
6.7 Formula Validation & Testing: Verifying overdue status indicators, days-to-deadline calculations, and error-handling on blank dates.
6.8 Knowledge Base Assembly: Populating core company knowledge pages: Company Overview, Team Directory, FAQs, and Tool Guides.
6.9 SOP Library Deployment: Writing 3 complete standard operating procedures: Client Onboarding, Project Kickoff, and Project Handover.
6.10 Operational Dashboard Assembly: Embedding linked views of Active Projects, Urgent Tasks, and Client Pipelines onto the homepage.
6.11 Intake Form Deployment: Connecting an intake form for client inquiries or internal service requests, routing records to triage.
6.12 Permission & Sharing Audit: Formulating the workspace permission matrix across Owner, Coordinator, Contributor, and Guest roles.
6.13 End-to-End System Testing: Simulating a live business cycle: new client intake → project kickoff → task assignment → completion.
6.14 Error Correction & Schema Optimization: Fixing broken relational links, cleaning up redundant properties, and optimizing view layouts.
6.15 Professional Handover Documentation: Compiling the Workspace Map, Database Schema Dictionary, User Guide, and Maintenance SOP.
6.16 Final Capstone Demonstration: Walking through the integrated workspace, defending schema choices, and presenting the verified system.
curriculum.hands_on_lab: Assemble, validate, and document the complete integrated Small-Business Notion Workspace & Knowledge System incorporating all 14 required portfolio components.
curriculum.deliverable: Small-Business Notion Workspace & Knowledge System — Final Capstone
curriculum.security_considerations: Verify zero public link leaks, confirm least-privilege role matrices, and validate that all test datasets contain synthetic information exclusively.

learning_outcomes: Explain Notion's workspace structure, block architecture, and cloud-synced document mechanics.
Navigate the Notion sidebar, command palette, breadcrumb trails, and search interfaces efficiently.
Create, structure, rename, duplicate, and archive Notion pages across personal and team spaces.
Utilize core Notion blocks including headings, callouts, lists, toggles, quotes, and columns.
Create organized nested pages with clean parent-child hierarchies, avoiding excessive nesting.
Organize business information logically using standardized naming conventions and clear content ownership.
Implement internal page links and @mentions to cross-reference related documentation seamlessly.
Create reusable page templates for recurring operational documents like meeting notes and client briefings.
Design a scalable information architecture connecting departments, projects, and administrative resources.
Create Notion databases in full-page and inline configurations tailored to operational tracking.
Define custom database properties with standardized schemas, naming rules, and data validation types.
Configure Status, Select, Multi-Select, Date, Person, Number, and Checkbox properties effectively.
Build customizable Table views with sorted columns, multi-condition filters, and property summaries.
Build interactive Board views (Kanban) grouped by workflow status or project ownership.
Build Calendar views based on project milestone dates and operational task deadlines.
Build Timeline views to visualize project scheduling, durations, and dependency sequences where supported.
Apply multi-condition AND/OR filter groups and multi-level sorting to surface actionable priorities.
Create linked database views across team pages to display contextual subsets of master data.
Distinguish master source databases from linked views, enforcing a single source of truth.
Connect disparate databases using Notion Relations (e.g., Clients to Projects, Projects to Tasks).
Create Notion Rollups to calculate progress metrics, aggregate completion counts, and inherit properties.
Write introductory Notion formulas using operators, property tokens, and conditional logic.
Build an operational client tracker supporting pipeline stages from lead intake to active retainer.
Build a project database tracking milestone target dates, project owners, and linked deliverables.
Build a task database linking action items to parent projects with assignees and due dates.
Link clients, projects, and tasks into a unified, relational three-tier small-business operational system.
Author comprehensive Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) with objectives, steps, checks, and owners.
Design a searchable company Knowledge Base organizing policies, FAQs, guides, and tooling resources.
Build reusable database templates to automate the creation of standard tasks, projects, and meeting notes.
Create clean, functional operations dashboards highlighting active projects, overdue tasks, and client stages.
Collaborate in Notion using inline comments, threaded discussions, @person tags, and page edits.
Create and deploy Notion Forms to capture stakeholder requests and route submissions into databases.
Implement interactive database buttons for rapid manual updates like completing tasks or adding notes.
Explain database automation limitations, trigger-action mechanics, and paid-tier subscription boundaries.
Configure workspace sharing, teamspace roles, member permissions, and guest access securely.
Distinguish filtered database views from actual access-control security to protect sensitive company records.
Explain Notion AI capabilities, Q&A search, drafting, database autofill, and plan-specific limits.
Understand autonomous agent concepts, October 2026 updates, credit allocations, and governance controls.
Test an end-to-end simulated small-business workspace across real operational lifecycles.
Compile professional workspace handover documentation including schema maps, user guides, and maintenance SOPs.

portfolio.title: Small-Business Notion Workspace & Knowledge System
portfolio.objective: Engineer one complete, fully operational Notion workspace for a simulated small service business, integrating relational client/project/task databases, an SOP library, a knowledge base, dashboard views, form intake, and permissions documentation.
portfolio.countingRule: One integrated small-business workspace containing 14 operational components demonstrating end-to-end knowledge and workflow management.

deliverables.title: Workspace Operational Homepage
deliverables.scenario: Construct the central small-business operational command center featuring quick navigation hubs, active project summary cards, urgent task views, and links to SOPs.
requirements: Organized navigation layout with clear branding and breadcrumb hierarchy.
Embedded linked views of high-priority operational databases.
Direct access pathways to Clients, Projects, Tasks, Knowledge Base, and SOPs.
Minimalist, functional design eliminating decorative clutter.

deliverables.title: Client Tracker Database
deliverables.scenario: Build a client relationship database tracking client profiles, pipeline stages, contact channels, account managers, and two-way relations to project records.
requirements: Properties: Client Name, Category, Status (Lead, Active, Archived), Account Owner, and Date Added.
Two-way relation link to the Projects database.
Table view for complete data management and Board view grouped by pipeline status.
Populated with realistic synthetic business client records.

deliverables.title: Project Management Database
deliverables.scenario: Design a project database tracking milestone target dates, progress statuses, project health, and relations to both parent clients and child tasks.
requirements: Properties: Project Name, Status, Priority, Start Date, Target Date, and Owner.
Two-way relations to Client Database and Task Database.
Rollups displaying total tasks count and percentage of tasks completed.
Timeline view (or Gantt alternative) and Board view by project phase.

deliverables.title: Task Management Database
deliverables.scenario: Engineer a granular task database tracking daily action items, due dates, assignees, priorities, and relations to parent projects.
requirements: Properties: Task Name, Status (To Do, In Progress, Done), Assignee, Due Date, and Priority.
Two-way relation linking each task to its parent project.
Introductory formula calculating Overdue warnings and Days Remaining.
Filtered views: 'My Tasks', 'Due This Week', and 'Overdue Items'.

deliverables.title: Working Relations & Rollups Architecture
deliverables.scenario: Verify and document the two-way relations and rollup calculations connecting Clients, Projects, and Tasks to guarantee single-source-of-truth integrity.
requirements: Client-to-Project two-way relation functioning accurately.
Project-to-Task two-way relation functioning accurately.
Minimum 2 verified Rollups (e.g., Task Count, Completion Percentage).
Minimum 1 working introductory formula property handling edge cases.

deliverables.title: Searchable Knowledge Base
deliverables.scenario: Author a centralized knowledge base categorizing organizational resources, team FAQs, company policies, and software tool guides.
requirements: Clear categorization structure (Operations, Team, Tools, Policies).
Searchable tags and standardized heading structure.
Cross-referenced links to active project docs and SOPs.
Document owner and last-reviewed date metadata on every knowledge page.

deliverables.title: Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Library
deliverables.scenario: Deploy an SOP library containing at least three complete, step-by-step procedures: Client Onboarding, Project Kickoff, and Project Handover.
requirements: Standardized SOP format: Purpose, Owner, Preconditions, Steps, QC Checks, and Review Date.
Formatted using callouts, toggles, checklists, and visual cues for clarity.
Direct linkage to relevant project and task database templates.
Minimum 3 fully authored operational procedures.

deliverables.title: Reusable Operating Templates
deliverables.scenario: Build pre-configured database templates that standardize the creation of new client records, project briefs, task checklists, and meeting notes.
requirements: New Client template with embedded onboarding checklist.
New Project template with auto-linked task views.
Meeting Notes template with agenda, attendee tags, and action items block.
SOP template enforcing the company's documentation standard.

deliverables.title: Executive Dashboard & Multi-View Hub
deliverables.scenario: Assemble an operational dashboard embedding linked views of active projects, upcoming deadlines, client pipeline stages, and quick-add actions.
requirements: Linked view of Projects filtered for 'Active' status.
Linked view of Tasks filtered for 'In Progress' or 'Due Soon'.
Board view of Client pipeline stages.
Clean visual layout optimized for daily morning standup reviews.

deliverables.title: Notion Form Request Intake
deliverables.scenario: Deploy a Notion Form for client inquiries or internal service requests, routing incoming responses directly into an intake database with data validation.
requirements: Logical form fields (Requester Name, Organization, Request Type, Urgency, Description).
Mandatory validation rules on required fields.
Direct connection to the Client or Task database for automatic row creation.
Documented manual fallback intake procedure.

deliverables.title: Collaboration & Permission Matrix
deliverables.scenario: Document an explicit permission strategy defining role-based access for Workspace Owners, Operations Coordinators, Team Contributors, and Client Guests.
requirements: Role definitions across 4 tiers: Owner, Member, Contributor, and Guest.
Page-by-page and database-by-database access permissions mapped out.
Documented explanation distinguishing filtered views from security boundaries.
Auditing checklist for external sharing and guest permissions.

deliverables.title: System Testing & Validation Report
deliverables.scenario: Execute a full simulation testing the entire workspace lifecycle from new client intake through task completion, logging all validation checkpoints.
requirements: Test Record Log: 5 clients, 8 projects, 20 tasks tested.
Verification of relation linkage and rollup calculation accuracy.
Testing of overdue formula output under simulated past-due dates.
Verification of form submission routing and guest permission barriers.

deliverables.title: Professional Workspace Handover Guide
deliverables.scenario: Author an operational handover manual for business stakeholders explaining workspace architecture, maintenance guidelines, and user training rules.
requirements: Visual Workspace Map showing page and database hierarchies.
Database Schema Dictionary detailing all properties, types, and relations.
Step-by-step instructions for onboarding new team members into the system.
Quarterly maintenance checklist for archiving stale data and auditing permissions.

deliverables.title: Responsible AI Governance Checklist
deliverables.scenario: Compile an operational policy governing the responsible, cost-aware use of Notion AI, agent review controls, and confidential data protection.
requirements: Guidelines for AI-assisted drafting, summarization, and search.
Human-in-the-loop verification protocol for dates, names, and financial figures.
Cost and credit management policy explaining plan tiers and spending limits.
Strict data confidentiality rules prohibiting real PII in prompts.

breakdown.area: Database design, views and data quality
Relations, rollups, formulas and connected workflows
Knowledge base, SOPs, collaboration and permissions
Capstone testing, AI awareness and handover

assessment_model.completionRule: Students must submit the complete integrated Small-Business Notion Workspace & Knowledge System. A visually elaborate workspace with disconnected databases, broken relations, non-functioning rollups, or insecure permission configurations will not receive passing evaluation.

faq.question: What is Notion — Workspace, Databases & Knowledge Systems?
faq.answer: A practical course covering Notion workspace design, databases, connected records, team documentation and collaboration.

faq.question: How long is the course?
faq.answer: Five weeks with 40 learning hours.

faq.question: What is the fee?
faq.answer: ₹5,900, subject to verified Nova Skills fee and tax policies.

faq.question: Is Notion suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. The course begins with pages, blocks and workspace organization.

faq.question: Do I need coding experience?
faq.answer: No.

faq.question: What is a Notion workspace?
faq.answer: A space for organizing pages, databases, documents and team information.

faq.question: What are Notion databases?
faq.answer: Structured collections of records with customizable properties and views.

faq.question: Will I learn database views?
faq.answer: Yes, including tables, boards, calendars and suitable supported views.

faq.question: What are linked database views?
faq.answer: Different views of records maintained in the same underlying source database.

faq.question: What are relations?
faq.answer: Properties that connect records across Notion databases.

faq.question: What are rollups?
faq.answer: Properties that summarize information from related database records.

faq.question: Will I learn Notion formulas?
faq.answer: Yes, at a practical introductory level.

faq.question: Will I create a client tracker?
faq.answer: Yes, using fictional or authorized records.

faq.question: Will I build a project tracker?
faq.answer: Yes, with a related task database.

faq.question: Is this a complete CRM certification?
faq.answer: No. It covers CRM-style tracking, not enterprise CRM implementation.

faq.question: Will I build a knowledge base?
faq.answer: Yes, including organized information and reusable documentation.

faq.question: Will I learn SOPs?
faq.answer: Yes, including documentation and reusable SOP templates.

faq.question: Are Notion Forms included?
faq.answer: Yes, with appropriate privacy safeguards.

faq.question: Are Notion Forms free?
faq.answer: Basic Forms are available across plans, while certain advanced capabilities require paid plans.

faq.question: Will I learn buttons?
faq.answer: Yes, including available basic actions and plan limitations.

faq.question: Are database automations free?
faq.answer: Most full database automation capabilities require paid plans.

faq.question: Will I learn team permissions?
faq.answer: Yes, including members, guests, page access and database access awareness.

faq.question: Do filtered database views protect confidential information?
faq.answer: Not by themselves. Actual access permissions must be configured appropriately.

faq.question: Will I learn Notion AI?
faq.answer: Yes, through responsible AI concepts and optional eligible demonstrations.

faq.question: Are Notion AI agents included?
faq.answer: Agent capabilities are covered conceptually, but access depends on plan, permissions and AI credits.

faq.question: Will I build a Custom Agent?
faq.answer: No advanced agent development is required.

faq.question: What changed in Notion AI in October 2026?
faq.answer: Notion expanded agent capabilities and connected workflows and introduced updated credit-management arrangements.

faq.question: Do I need a paid Notion subscription to complete the portfolio?
faq.answer: The core portfolio is designed around accessible functionality and approved instructor demonstrations; premium automations and AI are optional.

faq.question: What portfolio will I build?
faq.answer: A complete simulated small-business workspace with client/project/task databases, related records, knowledge base, SOPs, dashboards and permission documentation.

faq.question: Who should enroll?
faq.answer: Operations coordinators, freelancers, startups, administrators and professionals who need organized team knowledge and project tracking.
